title: AWS Lambda Cold Start Monitoring

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatchlogs` events with `("REPORT RequestId" OR "INIT_START")` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.56 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatchlogs` traffic without `("REPORT RequestId" OR "INIT_START")`. Confirm UC-4.1.56 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatchlogs` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs" ("REPORT RequestId" OR "INIT_START")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.56_aws_lambda_cold_start_mo_56"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.56 — AWS Lambda Cold Start Monitoring: queries AWS `aws:cloudwatchlogs` for search criteria `("REPORT RequestId" OR "INIT_START")` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'AWS Lambda Cold Start Monitoring' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.56 drives medium-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable CloudWatch Logs for Lambda (platform logs include REPORT and INIT). Optionally ingest X-Ray traces for end-to-end cold start visibility. Parse REPORT/INIT_START lines to extract init duration and invocation type. Alert when cold start rate exceeds 10% or init duration > 1s for critical functions. Consider provisioned concurrency for latency-sensitive workloads.
visualization: Line chart (cold start % and init duration by function over time), Table (function, cold starts, avg init ms), Single value (cold start rate).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where match(All_Changes.app, "(?i)glue|lambda|logs")
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.status span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Change / Performance: only if the TA maps job or platform logs; raw CloudWatch/CloudTrail is usually primary. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Known slow cold starts, scheduled batch jobs, and canary invocations in lower envs you already noise-reduced.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatchlogs`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable CloudWatch Logs for Lambda (platform logs include REPORT and INIT). Optionally ingest X-Ray traces for end-to-end cold start visibility. Parse REPORT/INIT_START lines to extract init duration and invocation type. Alert when cold start rate exceeds 10% or init duration > 1s for critical functions. Consider provisioned concurrency for latency-sensitive workloads.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs" ("REPORT RequestId" OR "INIT_START")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.56_aws_lambda_cold_start_mo_56"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatchlogs` in `index=aws` to detect aws lambda cold start monitoring. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_56_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (cold start % and init duration by function over time), Table (function, cold starts, avg init ms), Single value (cold start rate)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of aws lambda cold start monitoring so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
